rv.q: Phelim McDermott's production is full of invention, with neat puppetry and plenty of cheeky, lo-fi vibrancy.
The perfect, West End, family treat.
Pye's costumes are an eyeful and the whole thing's as luscious as it is ludicrous.

cn.t: Jim Broadbent leads a playful, inventive production that embraces theatrical artifice and toy-like charm. Critics praise the detailed performances and clever staging that sends up Victorian conventions while preserving the story's heart.
